hero.subtitle: A fall on someone else's property in Atascadero can leave you with medical bills and unanswered questions. We handle premises liability claims across San Luis Obispo County and can review your case at no cost.

about.title: Atascadero Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Atascadero's mix of downtown shops along El Camino Real, grocery stores on Morro Road, and older commercial buildings creates plenty of opportunities for wet floors, cracked pavement, and poorly lit stairwells. When a fall happens on someone else's property, California law generally requires you to show the property owner or manager knew, or should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn visitors. That standard makes the details matter: how long the spill sat there, whether an employee walked past it, what the surveillance camera captured before it's overwritten. Our team can start gathering evidence, evaluate notice, and explain your options under a contingency arrangement, meaning there's no fee unless you recover something.

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises law hinges on notice, so we can help pin down how long a hazard existed and who had a chance to address it before you fell.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many stores and businesses in Atascadero overwrite security footage within days or weeks, so acting quickly to preserve it can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Bar Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you're partly responsible for a fall, you may still recover a share of damages. We can help sort out how fault gets divided.

items.question: What if I fell but didn't take photos at the scene?
items.answer: Photos help, but they aren't the only evidence available. We can request incident reports, surveillance footage, and maintenance logs from the property, especially important for common Atascadero locations along El Camino Real and Morro Road where foot traffic is heavy on weekday afternoons.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If a government-owned property is involved, that window is much shorter, so it's worth having your situation reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Will I still have a case if I was partly at fault for the fall?
items.answer: Possibly. California follows pure comparative fault, which means your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of responsibility rather than eliminated entirely. We can help evaluate how that might apply to your specific circumstances.
